narrative:
The model estimates a 79% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who end up departing.

Three factors stood out as the strongest drivers of this prediction. First, your total years of professional experience (6–10 years) pushed the prediction most strongly toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have shorter experience (50% have only 1–5 years), your mid-range tenure appears to signal higher mobility in this dataset. Second, the fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the next biggest influence, pulling the outcome further toward departure. Third, your relatively short time in your current role (1–5 years) also contributed to the “will leave” direction, though less powerfully than the first two factors.

Taken together, these elements suggest the model views you as an experienced professional who is still early in your current position and already attracting external opportunities—conditions that frequently precede turnover.

Your organization should consider discussing retention measures with you, such as clearer promotion paths or expanded responsibilities. You, in turn, may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook the model currently sees. (218 words)
